candidates.title: Forensic anthropologists age a skeleton by its rib cartilage - ask whether an unguided CT model found the same clock
candidates.question: Does a chest-CT age model that was never told where to look recover the costal cartilage calcification clock, such that conditioning on calcified cartilage volume attenuates its age prediction more than conditioning on the aging markers a radiologist would name first?
candidates.deliverable_sentence: The chest-CT age model is using calcified costal cartilage volume - the same structure a forensic anthropologist scores to age an unidentified body - rather than aortic calcification, vertebral bone density or emphysema.

rung.why: Costal cartilage calcification is a structure a radiologist sees on every chest CT and has a name for, and its volume is a threshold measurement in cubic millimetres.
rung.what_would_move_it_up: Nothing above rung 3. What would strengthen it: showing the model's residual age error carries the sex-specific pattern the forensic literature describes, which is a hard-to-fake prediction - though see the contradiction flagged below, which weakens this test more than I would like.

X_measurement.X: Calcified costal cartilage volume - the volume of voxels above a fixed Hounsfield threshold inside the costal cartilage mask - reported both absolutely in cubic millimetres and as a fraction of total cartilage volume.
X_measurement.how: TotalSegmentator's default 'total' task, class 117 costal_cartilages, then threshold. Apache-2.0, no license key.
X_measurement.citations: Segmentation: Wasserthal J et al., Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2023, DOI 10.1148/ryai.230024, class map inspected directly in totalsegmentator/map_to_binary.py. Threshold and prior volumetry: Shabani M, Pishgar F, Akhtarkhavari S et al., Front Endocrinol 2021;12:785957, PMID 34966360, DOI 10.3389/fendo.2021.785957, in MESA at n=2,305: 'The volume of bilateral CCC was quantified in high-density pixels (threshold of Hounsfield Unit>180)'.
X_measurement.could_I_compute_it_today_without_asking_: Yes. Free tool, free class, a threshold, a voxel count.
X_measurement.published_age_gradient_to_calibrate_agai: MESA reports a '2.6% increase per each year [95%CI: 2.0-3.2%]' in females and '1.5% [1.0-2.1%]' in males, with median volume 1158 mm3 in females versus 3054 mm3 in males. Having a published per-year slope means the measurement can be validated before it is used to explain anything.

candidates.suspected_signal: Costal cartilage undergoes progressive dystrophic and metaplastic calcification through adult life, converting a structure that is invisible at soft-tissue window in a young adult into a high-attenuation, spatially extensive, bilaterally symmetric structure in an older one. It is a developmental clock rather than a disease marker, which is what distinguishes it from every aging feature a radiologist would name first - aortic calcification, vertebral height loss, emphysema, coronary calcium - all of which are pathological and therefore confounded by comorbidity rather than tracking chronology. It sits in the anterior chest, in the field of view of every chest CT ever acquired, at an attenuation that separates cleanly from surrounding soft tissue.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Costal cartilage can be segmented on ordinary ungated chest CT by a free tool, AND a public chest-CT corpus provides per-scan patient age across a range wide enough to fit an age model - so that a model's age prediction and a cartilage calcification volume exist for the same scans.
candidates.keystone_evidence: The first clause is INSPECTED_TRUE and is not the problem. TotalSegmentator's map_to_binary.py was read directly and the 'total' class map contains 116: 'sternum', 117: 'costal_cartilages'; the README confirms 'total: default task containing 117 main classes' and lists it among tasks 'Openly available for any usage (Apache-2.0 license)', unlike tissue_types, heartchambers_highres and coronary_arteries which require a license key. The second clause is NOT inspected and that is why the compound status is NOT_INSPECTED. The CT-CLIP paper reports a per-scan age range of 18 to 102 for CT-RATE, which is the wide span this candidate needs, but the metadata CSV column headers are behind the HuggingFace gate and returned HTTP 401; only VolumeName, RescaleSlope, RescaleIntercept, XYSpacing and ZSpacing are confirmed to exist, from the authors' own inference script. So I have confirmed that ages were RECORDED and not that a per-volume PatientAge column is RELEASED. As a Mode C candidate this cap is accepted rather than argued around, per the charter.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: Two, and the second is the one that would actually sink it. First, that TotalSegmentator's costal cartilage class performs acceptably on the corpus in question - it exists in the class map, which says nothing about its accuracy on a structure whose whole point is that it changes attenuation dramatically with age, and a segmenter that under-segments uncalcified cartilage in the young would manufacture the age gradient it is meant to measure. That failure mode is specific, plausible, and would produce a beautiful false positive. It must be checked by segmenting a fixed anatomical volume defined by rib and sternum landmarks INSTEAD OF by the cartilage mask, as a segmentation-independent replication. Second, that a chest CT reconstructed for diagnosis resolves the cartilage adequately at the slice thickness of the corpus. Neither is inspected.

rung_reached.conditional_on: The segmentation-independent replication agreeing with the mask-based measurement. Without it, the claim is about a segmentation tool rather than about anatomy.

candidates.dies_like_prior: It does not die like the annotation-provenance candidates: age is an administrative field recorded at registration, not a judgment anyone made by looking at the image, so there is no reader, no session, and no peer exposure. It does not die like idea 006, since nothing is ablated or edited. The failure mode it genuinely shares with idea 005 is the WRONG-KEYSTONE structure, and I am naming it rather than waiting for critique: the easy checkable fact is that a costal cartilage class exists, and I checked it and it is true; the fact my inference actually needs is that the class measures cartilage calcification rather than measuring the segmenter's own age-dependent behaviour. That is stated as the first residual assumption and it is, on reflection, the real keystone.

closest_prior_work.citation: Lu T, Deng ZH et al. Forensic age estimation based on costal cartilage CT using deep learning.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: n=2,700, ages 20 to 70, volume-rendered and maximum-intensity-projection multimodal deep learning: 'The best-performing multi-modality model obtained the lowest MAEs of 3.78 in males and 3.40 in females', against a manual visual scoring method at 8.90 and 6.42.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: This is the most dangerous prior work for the candidate and it must be confronted rather than minimized. It establishes that a model CAN estimate age from costal cartilage - but it TRAINED ON CROPPED COSTAL CARTILAGE RECONSTRUCTIONS, so the model was told exactly where to look. The question here is the inverse and it is the one this program exists to ask: does a model given a whole chest CT and only an age label FIND that structure on its own. Those are different claims, but the delta is narrower than I would like and a reviewer could reasonably say the interesting part - that cartilage carries age - is already known.

closest_prior_work.citation: Shabani M, Pishgar F, Akhtarkhavari S et al. Costal Cartilage Calcification in MESA.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Semi-automated HU>180 volumetry in 2,305 MESA participants with sex-stratified per-year age gradients, inter-reader reliability 88.7.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Uses the measurement as a cardiovascular risk marker on gated coronary-calcium scans, and the quantification is SEMI-automated with manual ROIs on a gated protocol. The open corner is fully automated volumetry on ordinary UNGATED chest CT - which is a narrow corner, and I would rather say so now than have it discovered in review. An entire MESA line follows this paper (Radiol Cardiothorac Imaging 2025 PMID 41342680; Acad Radiol 2025 PMID 40764198; Eur Radiol 2026 PMID 40782222), so the measurement itself is well occupied.

closest_prior_work.citation: MacPherson M, Goh V, Montana G et al. Deep learning age estimation from chest radiographs versus radiologists.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: The documented model-beats-human gap this candidate's entry point rests on: 'the regression model achieves an R2 of 0.94, MAE 3.53 years' against 'the radiologists achieve R2 of 0.27 with MAE 11.84 years'. Independently replicated in Japan by Ieki et al., Commun Med 2022, PMID 36494479, with seven clinicians at 'MAE 10.06 [95% CI, 9.17-10.94] years'.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Is on RADIOGRAPHS, not CT, and offers no explanation of the signal. NOT_FOUND, across three queries: any human-versus-model free age estimation on whole chest CT. The one adjacent CT comparison is anatomically narrow and shows essentially no gap once the human has a validated scoring system - Wesp et al., Int J Legal Med 2024, PMID 38286953, clavicle CT, model MAE 1.65 years versus human 1.84 years. So the gap motivating this candidate is borrowed from an adjacent modality, and if a human chest-CT baseline is needed it would have to be collected.

closest_prior_work.citation: Sipahioglu et al. Age estimation from chest CT with window-specific deep learning.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: n=1,278, ages 20 to 80, MAE 4.89 years, and reports that 'The bone-window model achieved the lowest MAE among single-window approaches, emphasizing the role of skeletal features', with Grad-CAM.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Points at skeletal features with a saliency method and a window ablation rather than measuring any quantity. It is the closest existing answer to this candidate's question and it stops precisely where measurement would begin - which is the standard failure this charter names.

closest_prior_work.citation: Rejtarova O et al., Forensic Sci Int 2009, PMID 19646830; Zhang S et al., Sci Rep 2017, PMID 28592818; Middleham et al., Clin Anat 2015, PMID 25534066.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Rejtarova established the sex-dimorphic ossification pattern - male 'peripheral ossification pattern', female 'central lingual ossification pattern' - and Zhang confirmed it on dual-energy CT in 154 patients: 'An increasing C pattern of cartilage was displayed in females, while P type preferred in males as age increased.'
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: And here is the contradiction I am not going to bury, because it damages the candidate's best identifiability test. Middleham et al. applied Rejtarova's method to 41 Scottish cadavers and sexed ZERO males correctly. Separately, Goh and Anderson, JBMR Plus 2025, PMID 39697522, report by pQCT that 'there was more calcification volume in cartilage of females than males' - the OPPOSITE direction to MESA's 1158 versus 3054 mm3. The sex-specific pattern is therefore not a reliable enough fingerprint to serve as the confirmatory test I originally wanted it to be, and identifiability is scored down accordingly rather than the test being quietly kept.

existing_assets: TotalSegmentator costal_cartilages in the free default task.
A published per-year age gradient in a 2,305-person cohort, sex-stratified, to validate the extractor against before it is used.
CT-RATE with a reported 18-to-102 age span and the CT-CLIP encoder, so an age model is a linear probe on frozen embeddings rather than a training run.

Competing mediators all measurable with the same free tool - aorta for calcification, vertebrae for trabecular attenuation, lungs for LAA%-950 - so the comparison set costs one extra segmentation pass.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Three stages, and the first is the go/no-go the keystone demands. Stage 0: confirm a per-volume age column is actually released, then run TotalSegmentator on 200 volumes spanning the age range and check that calcified cartilage volume reproduces the published per-year gradient of about 2.6 percent in females and 1.5 percent in males. If the extractor cannot recover a known, published, sex-stratified age slope, nothing downstream means anything and the candidate stops here. Stage 1: fit an age model as a linear probe on frozen CT-CLIP embeddings, which needs no training run and no architecture choices, and record its predictions on held-out scans. Stage 2, the actual question: mediation of the model's age prediction through calcified cartilage volume, against a pre-registered panel of competing mediators measured by the same tool - aortic calcification volume, vertebral trabecular attenuation, LAA%-950, and total heart volume. The claim is comparative, not absolute: cartilage must attenuate the prediction MORE than the markers a radiologist would name first, or the candidate has not earned its sentence. Stage 3, the segmentation-independent replication named in the residual: repeat the measurement inside a fixed anatomical box defined by rib and sternum landmarks rather than by the cartilage mask, to show the result is about anatomy rather than about the segmenter's age-dependent behaviour.

standing_confounds_addressed.scanner_and_vendor: PARTLY ADDRESSED by stratification, conditional on the metadata columns existing. A high-attenuation threshold measurement is less kernel-sensitive than a low-attenuation one, which helps.
standing_confounds_addressed.acquisition_protocol: NOT ADDRESSED. Contrast phase in particular could affect the threshold measurement at the cartilage boundary.
standing_confounds_addressed.reconstruction: PARTLY ADDRESSED - a 180 HU threshold on a high-contrast structure is far more kernel-robust than the minus 950 HU threshold C1 depends on, which is a real advantage of this X.
standing_confounds_addressed.positioning: ADDRESSED by construction - the measurement is defined by an anatomical mask, so it is invariant to where the patient sits in the frame.
standing_confounds_addressed.habitus: NOT ADDRESSED, and it is live: body size correlates with both cartilage volume and with age-related change. Mitigated by reporting the calcified FRACTION of cartilage as well as the absolute volume, since the fraction is size-normalized by construction.
standing_confounds_addressed.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE - the outcome is chronological age, which has no prevalence.
standing_confounds_addressed.referral_pathway: NOT ADDRESSED, and it matters more than usual here: who gets a chest CT is strongly age-dependent and indication-dependent, so the age distribution is not a population age distribution.
standing_confounds_addressed.label_leakage: PARTIALLY LIVE and worth naming - if age appears in the radiology report and the corpus's text was used in pretraining the encoder, an embedding-based age probe could be reading a textual association rather than an anatomical one. The linear probe is fit on IMAGE embeddings only, but CT-CLIP's image encoder was trained against report text, so this cannot be fully excluded and should be stated.

alternative_explanations: The segmenter, not the anatomy. Named as the real keystone above; addressed only by the Stage 3 landmark-box replication, and a positive result without that replication should not be believed.

Cartilage calcification is a proxy for general vascular and dystrophic calcification, so the model is reading calcium everywhere and cartilage is merely one convenient readout. PARTLY EXCLUDED by the competing-mediator panel, which includes aortic calcification specifically - but the two are correlated and the comparison is relative rather than clean.

Sex, not age. The measurement is strongly sex-dimorphic - by a factor of about 2.6 in MESA - and models predict sex from chest CT near ceiling, so an apparent age mediation could partly be a sex pathway. EXCLUDED only by fitting everything sex-stratified from the start, which must be pre-registered rather than added later.

Honest self-assessment. 'The model rediscovered the forensic anthropologist's clock' is the most seductive sentence in this portfolio and it is doing more work than the evidence will. Two things puncture it: a 2023 paper already showed deep learning can age costal cartilage, and MESA already showed the volumetry tracks age, so the genuinely new part is only that an UNGUIDED model converges on it. That is a narrower claim than the sentence implies, and I have scored novelty confidence 2 rather than dressing it up.

anticipated_negative.reasoning: Provided Stage 0 passes - the extractor reproduces the published age gradient - a null in Stage 2 is genuinely informative: it says that an unguided chest-CT age model is NOT using the structure that forensic science validated and that a bone-window ablation study pointed toward, which redirects the search to the competing mediators measured in the same pass. The comparative design is what makes the negative decisive rather than empty, because the competing mediators are measured simultaneously and one of them will be the answer. If Stage 0 fails, the study produces a feasibility result instead, which the charter also counts as success.

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: Age-at-death estimation from costal cartilage calcification in forensic anthropology and forensic radiology, where the marker has been scored on skeletons and post-mortem CT for decades.
cross_domain.measurement_it_implies: Segment costal cartilage, threshold at a fixed Hounsfield value, take the volume, stratify by sex, and compare against a published per-year gradient before using it for anything.
cross_domain.what_changes_if_the_analogy_is_dropped: The candidate becomes a different and worse study. Without forensic anthropology you would ask what a radiologist thinks makes a chest look old, and you would measure aortic calcification, vertebral height and bone density, emphysema, and thymic involution - every one of which is a DISEASE marker whose relationship to chronological age is mediated by comorbidity, so a positive would be uninterpretable between aging and illness. Forensic science's whole problem is estimating age in people about whom nothing else is known, which forced it toward markers that are developmental rather than pathological, and costal cartilage is the one that happens to sit inside a chest CT field of view. Concretely different code: you run TotalSegmentator's costal cartilage class and threshold at 180 HU, which nobody in radiology AI does, and you stratify by sex from the outset because the forensic literature says the pattern differs. It also supplied the sex-dimorphism confirmatory test - which, as recorded above, the same literature then undermined by contradicting itself. That is what a live analogy looks like as opposed to a decorative one: it changed the measurement, and it also cost me a test I wanted.

remaining_legwork: Confirm a per-volume age column exists in the gated CT-RATE metadata. Minutes after the gate, and it is the keystone.
Stage 0 extractor validation against the published MESA gradient on 200 volumes. One week including segmentation time.
Build the landmark-box replication measurement. One week, and it is not optional.
Fit the linear age probe on frozen embeddings and pre-register the mediator panel and sex stratification. One week.
Time to first decision: Stage 0 within two weeks, and it can kill the candidate before any modelling.

mechanism_clarity.why: A specific physical quantity - volume of voxels above 180 HU inside the costal cartilage - measured by a named free tool with a named class number, with a published per-year gradient in a 2,305-person cohort to validate against, and a named biological process for why it changes with age. This is the top of the rubric's description and I do not think it is arguable.

identifiability.why: The competing-mediator panel is measured in the same pass with the same tool, which is the design's strength, and the landmark-box replication separates anatomy from segmenter behaviour. But the mediation is observational, cartilage calcification correlates with vascular calcification, sex is a strong parallel pathway, and the sex-dimorphism test I wanted as confirmation is undermined by a direct contradiction in the source literature. Three is honest.

interest.why: A model given nothing but an age label converging on the marker forensic science spent decades validating is a genuinely good result, and the cross-domain route is not one this field would have taken. Held below 5 because a 2023 paper already aged costal cartilage with deep learning, so the surprise is about convergence rather than about the clock.

medical_relevance.why: Plausible utility rather than clear consequence. Understanding what a biological-age model reads matters for whether such scores mean anything clinically, and there is a real forensic application. But no management decision changes, and costal cartilage calcification is not itself actionable.

clarity.why: The question names the structure, the tool, the comparison set and the comparative criterion. Held below 5 because 'recovers the clock' is operationalized as relative mediation strength against a panel, which is a threshold-free comparison that will need a pre-registered decision rule to avoid being argued about afterwards.

feasibility.why: CAPPED at 3, keystone NOT_INSPECTED. The uncapped estimate would be about 3 anyway: TotalSegmentator over thousands of volumes is many GPU-hours, and Stage 0 could fail.

novelty_confidence.why: CAPPED at 3 but scored 2 on the evidence, which is a deliberate mark-down rather than a cap. MESA has semi-automated volumetry at n=2,305 and Eur Radiol has deep-learning age-from-cartilage at n=2,700, both with sex-stratified results. The residual gap is narrow - fully automated volumetry on ungated chest CT, used to explain an unguided model - and 'likely covered in part' is the honest reading.

data_readiness.why: Behind the CT-RATE click-through, with the needed column unverified.

evaluation_readiness.why: Mediation analysis is standard; a decision rule for 'recovers the clock' is not, and must be written.

negative_result_value.why: Decisive, conditional on Stage 0 passing, because the competing mediators are measured simultaneously.

regret.why: Worth considering. If it is true it is a lovely result, but nothing downstream is blocked by not knowing.

candidates.recommendation: DEVELOP FURTHER, DO NOT SHORTLIST YET - Stage 0 is cheap and the candidate should not be funded past it until the extractor reproduces the published age gradient.
unverified_claims: That CT-RATE releases a per-volume PatientAge column. The paper reports an 18 to 102 age range, so ages were recorded; the column list is gated and unread. This is the keystone.

That TotalSegmentator's costal cartilage class is accurate on ungated diagnostic chest CT, and specifically that its accuracy does not itself vary with the degree of calcification. This is the real keystone and it is unverified.
That the MESA per-year gradients transfer to an ungated non-cardiac-protocol corpus with different slice thickness.

That the sex-dimorphic ossification pattern is reliable. Two inspected sources contradict each other on the direction of the sex difference in volume, and a third failed to replicate the pattern for sex estimation entirely.
That a linear probe on frozen CT-CLIP embeddings gives a usable age model. Untested; the encoder was trained against report text rather than for age.
That no unguided-model age-attribution study exists. Searches did not cover forensic radiology conference proceedings, where this community publishes heavily.

candidates.title: Murray's cube law says how a branching tree should be built - ask whether the risk model is reading the lung's departure from it
candidates.question: Is the non-nodular part of Sybil's risk signal carried by pulmonary vascular pruning - small-vessel blood volume, and the departure of the arterial tree's caliber-ratio exponent from Murray's cube law - rather than by the parenchymal destruction that C1 proposes?
candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using pulmonary vascular pruning - the loss of blood volume in vessels below 5 square millimetres in cross-section, and the shift in the branching exponent away from the cube law that accompanies it - not parenchymal destruction.

rung.why: Vascular pruning is a named phenomenon with a named measurement that a thoracic radiologist recognizes, and the branching exponent is a physical quantity with a derivation.
rung.what_would_move_it_up: Nothing above rung 3. What the claim needs to be credible rather than higher: the exponent measurement validated against something, which currently does not exist at cohort scale - see the honest assessment below.

X_measurement.X: Two quantities, deliberately ordered by how much weight each can bear. PRIMARY, because it is validated: BV5, the aggregate blood vessel volume in vessels under 5 square millimetres cross-section, normalized to total blood vessel volume. SECONDARY, because it is the mechanism but the measurement is immature: the caliber-ratio exponent k fitted from parent and daughter radii at detected bifurcations, r_parent^k = sum of r_daughter^k.
X_measurement.how: TotalSegmentator's free lung_vessels task gives lung_arteries, lung_veins, lung_airways and lung_airways_wall - confirmed Apache-2.0 and free, and the README cites Sci Data 2025 s41597-025-06074-6 and arXiv:2404.03010 for it. Cross-sectional area binning for BV5 is not provided off the shelf and must be implemented, or ChestImagingPlatform used, which is source-build only with no pip or conda package and a custom non-OSI license. The exponent additionally requires skeletonization, bifurcation detection and per-branch radius estimation.
X_measurement.citations: BV5 definition and original: San Jose Estepar R, Washko GR et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2013;188(2):231-239, PMID 23656466, PMC3778757, defining it as 'the aggregate vessel volume for vessels less than 5 mm2' and concluding that 'Smoking-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is characterized by distal pruning of the small blood vessels (<5 mm2) and loss of tissue in excess of the vasculature.' Mortality anchor: Synn AJ, Rice MB et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2021;203(2):251-254, PMID 32926788, Framingham n=2,470: 'Each SD lower BV5/TBV (i.e., more severe pruning) was associated with a 35% greater rate of death (HR, 1.35; 95% CI, 1.09-1.68; P = 0.006).' Histologic validation: Synn AJ et al., Pulm Circ 2021, PMID 34881020, n=138, correlation of BV5/TBV with vessel wall area percent of minus 0.41. Exponent reference: Altieri Correa S, Chesler NC et al., J Biomech Eng 2025;147(8):081006, PMID 40489106.
X_measurement.could_I_compute_it_today_without_asking_: BV5, yes with implementation work - the segmentation is free and the binning is geometry. The exponent, yes in principle and not reliably in practice at the vessel calibres that matter on low-dose screening CT. That distinction is the candidate's central feasibility problem and it is why BV5 is primary.

candidates.suspected_signal: Murray's law follows from minimizing the sum of two costs: the viscous power dissipated driving flow through a tube, which falls steeply with radius, and the metabolic cost of maintaining the blood it contains, which rises with radius. Minimizing the total gives flow proportional to radius cubed, hence a conserved cube of radius across a bifurcation. Smoking-related vascular remodeling destroys and narrows the distal small vessels first - the pruning that BV5 measures directly - which changes the ratio of maintenance cost to dissipation cost the tree is optimizing, and therefore shifts the exponent away from the healthy value. So the exponent is not a redescription of pruning; it is a scale-free summary of the same remodeling that is invariant to overall lung size and to inflation level, where BV5 is a bulk volume that is not. Pruning is in turn a plausible substrate for cancer risk through chronic hypoxia, impaired immune surveillance in underperfused parenchyma, and its established association with mortality.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Pulmonary arterial and venous trees can be segmented from NLST low-dose screening CT by a free tool at sufficient fidelity that per-vessel cross-sectional area can be binned, and bifurcations resolved, in the calibre range where pruning occurs.
candidates.keystone_evidence: What is established: TotalSegmentator's lung_vessels task exists, is free under Apache-2.0, and outputs lung_arteries and lung_veins as separate classes - read directly from map_to_binary.py. What is NOT established, and is exactly what the inference needs: its performance on LOW-DOSE screening CT at 1 to 2.5 mm slice thickness, in vessels around and below 2 mm diameter, which is at the resolution limit. No off-the-shelf calibre binning exists in that tool. ChestImagingPlatform, the public descendant of the software the BV5 literature actually used, has no pip or conda package and no tagged releases - the README defers dependency resolution to an external link - and the original BV5 paper used 'in-house software' rather than CIP. Mode C permits this status and I am reporting it rather than working around it.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: Having established that a free vessel segmenter exists, I am still assuming the entire measurement chain downstream of it: that cross-sectional area can be estimated per vessel segment accurately enough to bin at a 5 square millimetre boundary on low-dose data, and - for the secondary quantity - that radii at bifurcations can be estimated well enough to fit an exponent. The second assumption is almost certainly too optimistic, and the literature says so implicitly: the ENTIRE human evidence base for a pulmonary Murray exponent is about 23 subjects across two papers, reporting 2.31 +/- 0.60 and 2.92 +/- 1.07. Those standard deviations exclude essentially nothing, on hand-curated angiographic geometries, which is a strong signal that the measurement is hard even under favourable conditions. I would rather state that the exponent is the mechanism and BV5 is the measurement than pretend both are equally available.

rung_reached.conditional_on: BV5 carrying the result. If only the exponent moves and BV5 does not, the finding should be treated as a measurement artifact until independently replicated, given how underpowered the exponent literature is.

candidates.dies_like_prior: No annotation-provenance failure applies - both quantities are computed from voxels by tools, and the model score is a checkpoint output. No intervention-validity failure applies, because nothing is edited. The candidate's own most likely death is neither of those: it is that the measurement is not achievable at the resolution of low-dose screening CT, which is a feasibility death rather than a validity death, and Mode C exists to permit exactly that risk. The one prior pattern it does share is scout-003's dropped question 7, which died because a pulmonary vascular class could not be confirmed in a released segmentation output. That specific blocker is now resolved - lung_vessels exists and is free - so the vascular question has advanced one step in two cycles, from 'no tool confirmed' to 'tool confirmed, fidelity unknown'.

closest_prior_work.citation: San Jose Estepar R, Washko GR et al. Computed Tomographic Measures of Pulmonary Vascular Morphology in Smokers and Their Clinical Implications.
closest_prior_work.identifier: Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2013;188(2):231-239, PMID 23656466, PMC3778757
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Defined BV5, established distal pruning in smoking-related COPD in 359 smokers and 82 never-smoker controls.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Relates the measurement to disease, not to any model. Critically for this cycle, it also reports that '%LAA-950 was inversely related to all calculated vascular ratios' - which is the single most important sentence for the C1-versus-C5 comparison, because it means the two candidates' named explanations move together and a positive for either is weak evidence against the other. Any design that runs both must report partial associations, not marginal ones.

closest_prior_work.citation: Altieri Correa S, Kachabi A, Colebank MJ, Miles CE, Chesler NC. Revisiting Murray's Law in Pulmonary Arteries.
closest_prior_work.verification: INSPECTED (abstract; the human-cohort modality detail is SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY)
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Measured the exponent across four species: 'an average exponent value of 2.31(+/-0.60) in human... all lower than the predicted value of 3.0 from Murray's Law.' Human n=7, on geometries reported by a search summary to be mixed CT and MR angiography.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: n=7 humans on curated angiographic geometries. It gives the candidate a reference value and simultaneously warns that the measurement is imprecise. Corroborating and diverging: Dong M, Marsden AL, Feinstein JA et al., Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol 2020, PMID 32618514, n=16, reports 2.92 +/- 1.07. Theory permits the departure - Kassab GS, 2006, PMID 16143652: 'The exponent of the diameter-flow rate relation is not necessarily equal to 3.0 as required by Murray's law but depends on the ratio of metabolic to viscous power dissipation.' NOT_FOUND across four queries: any human study measuring a pulmonary Murray exponent in COPD, smoking, pulmonary hypertension or fibrosis. The only disease-related shift is ovine - Ghorishi Z, Eldridge MW et al., 2007, PMID 17308003, where shunt-hypertensive lambs retain the fetal exponent.

closest_prior_work.citation: Helmberger M, Olschewski H, Balint Z et al. Quantification of Tortuosity and Fractal Dimension of the Lung Vessels in Pulmonary Hypertension Patients.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Measured 3D fractal dimension and tortuosity of the pulmonary vascular tree on contrast CT.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Found 3D fractal dimension NOT significantly different in pulmonary hypertension, with only tortuosity tracking mean pulmonary artery pressure. This directly contradicts a 2D fractal dimension result - Sun H et al., Korean J Radiol 2011, PMID 21603288, reporting 1.64 versus 1.54 - and the inconsistency is a warning that geometric summaries of this tree are unstable across methods. It is the reason the exponent is secondary here.

closest_prior_work.citation: Mikhael et al. JCO 2023 and Sobieski et al. arXiv:2602.02560, as detailed under C1.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Established the non-nodular residual signal and audited nodule contributions.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Neither paper measures anything vascular. The audit paper's speculation names emphysema, not pruning - so this candidate is proposing an explanation nobody has put in print, which is the point of Mode C and also the reason it carries more risk than C1.

existing_assets: TotalSegmentator lung_vessels, free and Apache-2.0, with separate artery and vein classes - the blocker that killed this question in the previous cycle.
Sybil weights under MIT and NLST imaging under CC BY 4.0, shared with C1, so the model and data cost nothing beyond what C1 already pays.
A mature outcome-anchored literature for BV5 including a Framingham mortality hazard ratio and histologic validation, so the biomarker's meaning does not have to be argued from scratch.
A published human reference value for the exponent, with honest uncertainty attached.
If C1 runs, the entire pipeline except the vessel analysis already exists, which is the strongest practical argument for running this as an arm of C1 rather than as a separate study.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Stage 0 is a pure feasibility probe and it decides everything: run TotalSegmentator lung_vessels on 50 NLST low-dose scans and 50 matched diagnostic-quality chest CTs, and measure whether the artery and vein trees are recovered to a consistent depth and whether cross-sectional areas can be estimated stably around the 5 square millimetre boundary. Report the calibre at which recovery degrades. If the tree is only reliable above 5 square millimetres, BV5 is not measurable on this data and the candidate stops - a feasibility result the charter counts as success, and one that would also tell the vascular-imaging community something useful about applying a free tool to screening CT. Stage 1, if Stage 0 passes: compute BV5 normalized to total blood vessel volume on held-out nodule-free NLST scans at fixed kernel, and estimate its association with Sybil's score. Stage 2 is the only analysis that distinguishes this candidate from C1 and it must be pre-registered as the primary comparison rather than an add-on: compute LAA%-950 on the same scans and report the PARTIAL association of the score with each, conditional on the other. Given that the two are known to be inversely related, marginal associations would produce two positives and no answer. Stage 3, exploratory and labelled as such: fit the branching exponent on the subset where the tree is recovered deeply enough, and ask whether it adds anything after BV5 - with the pre-registered expectation that it probably will not, and that a positive here without a BV5 positive should be disbelieved.

standing_confounds_addressed.scanner_and_vendor: PARTLY ADDRESSED by stratification. Vessel segmentation fidelity varies with scanner and reconstruction more than a bulk density measure does, which makes this worse here than in C1.
standing_confounds_addressed.acquisition_protocol: NOT ADDRESSED beyond stratification. NLST is non-contrast, which is a genuine limitation for vessel work - most of the BV5 literature and all of the exponent literature uses better-contrasted or contrast-enhanced data.
standing_confounds_addressed.reconstruction: PARTLY ADDRESSED by fixing the kernel, and the same paired-kernel manipulation available to C1 applies here and should be used - if BV5 shifts across kernels the way LAA-950 does, the same discipline is required.
standing_confounds_addressed.site: NOT ADDRESSED AND NOT ADDRESSABLE, per the masked screening centre.
standing_confounds_addressed.positioning: PARTLY ADDRESSED - the measurement is defined on a segmented tree rather than on fixed coordinates. But gravity-dependent perfusion differences between dependent and non-dependent lung are real and are not removed.
standing_confounds_addressed.habitus: NOT ADDRESSED. Body size affects both vessel volume and image noise, and noise affects small-vessel recovery. Mitigated by normalizing BV5 to total blood vessel volume, which is the convention the source literature uses for exactly this reason.
standing_confounds_addressed.prevalence: ADDRESSED by construction, single screening cohort.
standing_confounds_addressed.label_leakage: NOT APPLICABLE - no labels in the primary readout.
standing_confounds_addressed.inflation_level: NOT ADDRESSED and specific to this candidate: bulk vessel volume depends on how inflated the lung is, which C3 shows is uncontrolled in any single-scan corpus. The exponent is scale-free and therefore immune, which is the one respect in which the secondary quantity is better than the primary one - and it is the concrete reason the Murray framing is not decorative.

alternative_explanations: Parenchymal destruction, i.e. C1's explanation. NOT EXCLUDED by design, only by partial association, because the two quantities are inversely correlated by the source literature's own report. This is the candidate's central identifiability problem and it is why C1 and C5 should probably be run as one study with two named mediators rather than as two studies.

Vessel segmentation fidelity varying with disease severity. Emphysematous lung has less contrast around vessels, so the segmenter may recover fewer small vessels in exactly the patients who are sickest - which would manufacture the pruning association from a tool artifact. This is the same shape of failure as C4's segmenter risk and it is at least as likely here. PARTLY EXCLUDED by reporting recovery depth as a covariate and by the Stage 0 calibre-degradation curve.
Noise. Small-vessel recovery on low-dose CT is noise-limited, and noise scales with body size and with automatic exposure control. PARTLY EXCLUDED by including effective mAs as a covariate.

Honest self-assessment. Murray's law is the most attractive-sounding idea in this portfolio and the one most at risk of being decoration. The charter's test is what would change if the analogy were dropped, and the answer is given under cross_domain below - it is a real answer, involving different code and a specific invariance property. But I want to be plain that the exponent is very unlikely to be measurable at NLST resolution, that its human evidence base is 23 subjects, and that if this candidate produces a result it will almost certainly be a BV5 result with the exponent as an unfalsified aside. Anyone reading the title should read that sentence too.

anticipated_negative.reasoning: Conditional on Stage 0 passing, a null in Stage 2 - BV5 showing no partial association with Sybil's score once LAA%-950 is conditioned on - is decisive for the vascular hypothesis and simultaneously strengthens C1's parenchymal one, because the two are tested against each other on the same scans in the same model. That is the value of running competing named explanations jointly: neither can produce an uninterpretable null, because the alternative is measured in the same breath. If Stage 0 fails the result is a feasibility finding about applying free vessel segmentation to low-dose screening CT, which is useful and publishable but is not an answer to the question asked.

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: Optimal-transport scaling laws for biological distribution networks - Murray's 1926 minimization of viscous dissipation plus metabolic maintenance cost, and its descendants in allometric scaling theory - which predict a conserved power of radius across every bifurcation of a well-built tree.
cross_domain.measurement_it_implies: Do not measure how much vasculature there is. Measure the RATIO between parent and daughter calibres at bifurcations, and fit the exponent that makes it conserved. That is a scale-free quantity: it does not change if the lung is bigger, and it does not change if the patient inhaled more deeply.
cross_domain.what_changes_if_the_analogy_is_dropped: You measure BV5 and stop. BV5 is a bulk volume, so it inherits every problem that C3 exists to demonstrate: it depends on how inflated the lung was, on body size, and on total lung volume, and none of those are controlled in a single-scan corpus. The scaling-law framing says the informative quantity is a ratio at a junction, which is invariant to all three by construction, and it supplies a predicted value - 3 for laminar flow - that the measurement can be checked against rather than merely reported. Concretely different code: skeletonize the segmented tree, detect bifurcations, estimate radii on both sides, fit an exponent - none of which appears in a BV5 pipeline. It also generates a falsifiable prediction the bulk measure cannot: the exponent should be stable across C3's inflation states while BV5 should not, which is a test that can actually be run on the CT-vs-PET breath-hold pairs. That test is the strongest evidence that the analogy is load-bearing rather than ornamental, and it costs one extra analysis on data another candidate is already downloading.

remaining_legwork: Stage 0 vessel-recovery feasibility probe on 50 low-dose and 50 diagnostic scans. Two weeks including segmentation time, and it is a hard go/no-go.
Implement calibre binning, since no free tool provides it. Two to three weeks.
Decide whether to build ChestImagingPlatform from source as a reference implementation, given no pip package and a custom license. One week, possibly wasted.
If Stage 3 is attempted: skeletonization and bifurcation radius estimation. A month, with a high chance of producing a number nobody should believe.
Time to first decision: Stage 0 in about two weeks, and it is likely to be the decision.

mechanism_clarity.why: Two specifically named physical quantities with derivations and measurement definitions, one of them - BV5 - validated against histology and anchored to a mortality hazard ratio in Framingham. Held below 5 because the quantity that carries the MECHANISM, the exponent, does not have a usable measurement at this resolution, and the quantity that has a usable measurement is a bulk volume whose mechanistic story is thinner. A candidate whose mechanism and whose measurement sit on different variables is not at the top of this scale.

identifiability.why: The partial-association design against C1's named alternative is genuinely discriminating, and the inflation-invariance prediction is a real test that can be run on C3's data. But BV5 and LAA-950 are known to be inversely correlated, segmentation fidelity plausibly varies with the disease being measured, and the whole thing is observational. Three.

interest.why: Proposing a vascular rather than parenchymal explanation for a documented gap is a genuine claim nobody has published, and it serves the charter's named vascular emphasis, which has gone unfilled for two cycles. Held below 5 because the likely outcome is a feasibility wall rather than an answer.

medical_relevance.why: Pruning is outcome-anchored - a 35 percent higher death rate per standard deviation in Framingham - and unlike emphysema it is not something a radiologist reads off a screening CT today, so a positive would point at a finding that is currently invisible in practice. Held below 5 because nothing in management changes on this result alone.

clarity.why: The question names two quantities, the competing explanation, and the comparison. Held below 5 because carrying a primary and a secondary X makes the claim compound, and a result that splits between them will be harder to state in one sentence than the deliverable implies.

feasibility.why: CAPPED at 3, scored 2 on the evidence. Vessel segmentation on non-contrast low-dose screening CT at the calibres that matter is the hardest measurement in the portfolio, no free tool does calibre binning, and the reference implementation has no installable package. Mode C explicitly forbids demoting the candidate for this, and the score here is reported outside the priority calculation for that reason.

novelty_confidence.why: CAPPED at 3, and 3 is also the honest estimate. No human study measures a pulmonary Murray exponent in disease, and no study relates vascular pruning to a lung cancer risk model. But BV5 is a well-worked field with an active group, and a pruning-versus-Sybil analysis is a natural thing for that group to do next.

data_readiness.why: Shared with C1: CC BY 4.0 imaging, MIT weights, public outcomes, no gate.

evaluation_readiness.why: BV5 has published conventions but no accessible reference implementation; the exponent has no accepted CT measurement protocol at all. Unclear, and much would have to be invented.

negative_result_value.why: Decisive conditional on Stage 0, because the competing explanation is measured simultaneously on the same scans.

candidates.sibling_disclosure: C5 and C1 share Sybil, NLST, the held-out split, the kernel discipline and the nodule-free population, and they propose COMPETING explanations for the same residual signal. They are not independent bets and a reviewer should not count them as two. My recommendation is explicit: do not fund them separately. Run C1, and add BV5 as a second pre-registered mediator inside it, with the partial-association analysis as the primary comparison. That gets the scientific benefit of the competition - neither explanation can produce an uninterpretable null when the other is measured alongside it - at a fraction of the cost, and it removes the temptation to report whichever marginal association came out larger.

regret.why: If the answer is vascular and everyone spends five years measuring parenchyma because one ICML paper wrote the word emphysema in a speculative sentence, that would be a costly and avoidable wrong turn. The regret is real; the probability of getting to an answer is what is low.

candidates.recommendation: DO NOT SHORTLIST AS A STANDALONE STUDY. Run Stage 0 as a two-week feasibility probe, and if it passes, fold BV5 into C1 as a competing mediator rather than running this separately. The Murray exponent should be carried as an explicitly exploratory arm and reported as such however it comes out.
unverified_claims: That TotalSegmentator lung_vessels recovers vessels at the calibres BV5 requires, on non-contrast low-dose screening CT. Completely untested and it is the keystone.
That cross-sectional area can be estimated stably enough to bin at 5 square millimetres on this data.
That the branching exponent is measurable at all from NLST-quality data. I doubt it, and I have said so rather than letting the title imply otherwise.
The modality of the human geometries in Altieri Correa et al. A search summary indicates mixed CT and MR angiography; the methods section could not be opened.
That ChestImagingPlatform builds from source in a reasonable time. No pip package, no tagged releases, custom license.
That vessel segmentation fidelity does not itself vary with emphysema severity. Untested, and it is the most plausible route to a false positive.

That no BV5-versus-risk-model analysis exists. The BV5 literature is concentrated in a small number of groups and searches did not cover ATS or thoracic society abstracts, where that community publishes first.
